newsitem.title: INDIA: Mandela sees trade with India passing $2 billion.
newsitem.headline: Mandela sees trade with India passing $2 billion.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said on Friday he expected annual bilateral trade with India to pass $2 billion in the next three years.

"We are greatly encouraged by the interest which South African mining and engineering companies have shown in what India offers in the field of mining and infrastructure development," Mandela told a meeting of Indian businessmen.
"We expect relations in banking, shipping, insurance and tourism to grow in the near future," he said on the second day of a three-day visit to India.

"We have only just begun to build the relationships which our joint freedom makes possible. There is no reason why trade should not reach $2 billion a year and more by the year 2000, or why investments in both directions should not be at corresponding levels," he said.
Indo-South African trade touched $220 million in 1994/95 (April-March) and had reached $260 million in the first half of 1995/96, officials said.

Mandela's visit concided with the launch of South Africa's strategic partnership with India on Friday, seeking economic cooperation in shared Indian Ocean waters and democratic reforms in the United Nations for equal powers to all nations.
Mandela, on his third visit to India, and Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda signed the declaration at Delhi's 17th-century Red Fort during a reception in honour of the South African leader.

"Convinced that the United Nations structures needed to be more representative of the concerns and diversities of the developing world, India and South Africa re-emphasise their belief in the need for U.N. reforms," the United News of India quoted the declaration as saying.

"We are in favour of a drastic restructuring of the (United Nations) Security Council," Mandela earlier told a news conference. He said U.N. members should have equal powers and not be restrained by vetoes enjoyed by a few.

The joint declaration expressed the two nations' resolve to coordinate efforts to make the recently-formed Indian Ocean Rim Association for Regional Cooperation "an instrument of substantive partnership", the Press Trust of India said.
The two countries have been leading efforts to form the basis for a free-trade bloc of Indian Ocean Rim countries.

"The economies of India and South Africa have certain comparative advantages, complementarities and resources which can be optimally used to promote economic development thorugh cooperation," the declaration said.
It said the two countries recognised South Africa's geostrategic location as a transshipment point between Asia, Africa and Latin America.
Mandela said he expected India to support South Africa's bid to host the Olympic Games in Cape Town in 2004.
"I have no doubt that if we make a bid, whether we ask India or not, they will support us," he said.
